text:
sasha: quick question — we saw a customer hit a weird case where streaming responses keep producing tokens after the client triggers an AbortController in the browser. node sdk seems to stop, python keeps reading a few more chunks, go closes gracefully but server logs show repeated retry attempts. anyone seen this mix of behaviors?

devon: yep saw on a support ticket. likely a mismatch between client-side abort semantics and our server retry/backoff. are they using resumable retries or automatic fallback?

sasha: they're on hosted API, no explicit resumable. just plain streaming with a client abort. repro steps: start a streaming completion, then call `controller.abort()` immediately when user cancels. browser shows streaming websocket close, server logs a 499-ish cancel then a few subsequent attempt logs like we retried request 1 and 2.

kai: two places to check: 1) client library must propagate `signal` into underlying http/stream call (node fetch, requests, net/http). 2) server-side should treat aborts as terminal for that request_id and not re-enqueue. if we have automatic server-side retries without idempotency key, can double-work.

maria: from the SDK side: node implementation wires AbortController down to underlying fetch and closes the HTTP/2 stream. example we recommend: 
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
client.stream({ model: 'x', input }, { signal: ac.signal })
// later
ac.abort();
```
but we had race where cancel fires while initial headers not sent -> transport keeps trying. we should ensure a short client-side timeout before attempting retry.

tim: in python we wrap sockets with `asyncio.CancelledError` propagation. but some upstream libs swallow the cancellation and drain remaining chunks. we added an explicit `stream.close()` call in our wrapper to force socket close. might be missing in customers' code.

andre: infra-bot flagged three incidents where `retry-manager` retried on network errors including `ClientDisconnected` which is our internal code for aborted sockets. that's bad. we should make `ClientDisconnected` non-retryable. filing follow-up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/512

devon: agree. also adding an idempotency header `x-rw-request-id` from clients helps server decide when retries are safe. if missing, server may attempt best-effort retries which produce duplicate work.

kai: proposal: unify conventions across SDKs:
- clients MUST send `x-rw-request-id` for streaming requests (generated client-side)
- aborts should map to non-retryable terminal codes (`ClientAbort`) on server
- streaming cancellation handshake: client sends FIN/close then server must send a `stream-cancelled` event and stop requeuing

maria: +1. implementation notes per-sdk: node: AbortController -> fetch.signal -> close connection early; python: `await stream.aclose()` then raise CancelledError; go: context cancel on request then `req.Body.Close()` and return non-retryable err. we should publish small snippets in SDK docs.

sasha: nice. quick sync: who can own changes? i'll open RFC for behavior, but we need one PR per repo (node, python, go) and a server change to make `ClientDisconnected` non-retryable.

tim: i can take python SDK PR. will add example and tests for streaming cancel and ensure we call `aclose()` on cancel.

devon: i'll take node SDK PR. plan: ensure signal travels to underlying http2 client, add integration test using a fake slow server that asserts socket closed immediately on abort.

kai: assigning infra change to me — will update retry-manager config and add a short-circuit for `ClientDisconnected` and add a metric to count aborted-but-retried events.

andre: infra-bot: queued incident follow-ups: (1) platform PR 512 referenced, (2) add metric alert if aborted-but-retried > 0 over 5m, (3) backfill customer logs to find affected tenants.

maria: linking potential SDK PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/stream-abort.md

sasha: awesome. next steps: devon/tim/kai create PRs by EOD Wed, i'll draft RFC and coord with support for customer repro. also add tiny doc in devex about cross-sdk abort semantics. cc @andre for infra changes. :thumbsup:

devon: quick question: should client-generated `x-rw-request-id` be stable across reconnects for the same logical user action? my thinking: yes for dedupe on server if retry happens, but ephemeral per attempt for safety?

kai: make it stable per logical attempt (i.e., per user action). on reconnects where the client explicitly retries same operation, keep same id. on new user actions, generate new id. document this.

tim: noted. i'll add tests for same-id dedupe = server should not re-execute model compute if sees identical id within 30s window.

sasha: sweet. i'll update the support ticket and paste this thread. thanks all.
